entry_points.text: Init aborts without usable or enabled hyp mode, else prepares tables, limits, vectors and VMIDs before hyp setup and registration, finalizing protected state or unwinding on failure.
Table setup validates order and uniqueness including GIC extension, then implementation regs, nested forwarding, feature coverage and per-register config, failing on any error.
Nested S2 helper clears fault, returns immediately when nested inactive, else builds controls from registers and delegates to traversal preserving non-fault bits on failure.

exports.text: MPIDR lookup under RCU returns vCPU for masked affinity or null; fast table with validation first, else full scan.
Bypass and routing hooks with irqchip predicate; only MSI routes forward, identical message updates ignored, other changes release direct state.

Direct forwarding setup and teardown with ITS resolution; unsupported or unresolvable cases succeed silently preserving emulation. Valid doorbells need ITS device via bus, valid device and mapped collection with LPIs enabled; descriptors carry VM state, target element, ID, priority properties and doorbell enable. vLPI flag tracks emulated versus forwarded with host number and count, migrating pending on establish and releasing on teardown; translation fails on disabled ITS, unknown device or event, unmapped collection, missing target or disabled LPIs.
Executable identity map of hyp text with logged failure propagation.
Forwarding registration stores index-plus-one by encoding rejecting range and duplicate errors; GICv3 accessor publishes table with count.
VMID init discovers usable width, warns when space barely exceeds CPUs with zero reserved, seeds generation and bitmap; free releases bitmap.
AT swap needs caller-held SRCU, resolves slot for IPA, checks host address and writability, performs capability-selected 8-byte CAS then marks dirty on success.

hazards.text: Atomic routing changes cannot sleep so material message updates only tear down direct state; bypass stop halts guest and start resumes it.
Systems with certain load-acquire errata warn untrusted guests lacking workarounds may deadlock and should be restricted to trusted images.

invariants.text: IPA width derives from sanitized PARANGE capped without large addressing; SVE guest length clamps to virtualizable and architectural maxima with host max recorded separately.

52-bit handling widens output masks when granule and feature allow; nested output checked against max except 48 passes all; fault status low bits encode level; descriptor addresses assemble extra high bits when large.
Collection mapped only with handle and non-sentinel target; LPIs enabled by redistributor control; devices own entries linking collections to virtual interrupts resolved via target address.
Cache key combines device high by typer width with event; caching best-effort never direct with exclusive ownership and race tolerance; reverse scan finds direct LPIs and takes a reference.

Feature tables cover all non-reserved bits; nested trap base rejects reserved, duplicate, bad group, reserved fine and recursive combos; FGT bits accumulate by polarity into positive and negative sets with reserved views, must partition width, overlapping claims fail while non-partitioning sets heal after logging.

Sysreg order lexicographic over five fields with null last; audit needs strict increase and optional reset handlers else aborts; boot IDs snapshotted; mode and WFI/WFE parsers accept known values honoring VHE and hyp presence.

AT regime from operation with E2H and TGE at EL2; TCR2 zero without nested support; PIE and POE need advertisement with EL0 overlay excluded in pure EL2; granule validated against features with fallback preferring host size.

S1 setup selects controls by regime and range, derives shift, large-address, start level and shareability, validates tagging, uses identity path when disabled or enforces constraints; walk strides by page shift with nested retry, filter abort, leaf rules, atomic access-flag update and endianness handling. Context holds regime, size, granule, limits, shareability, endianness, flags, base, update state, start level and EL0 access with result fault, level and address.

Nested S2 controls from virtualization regs and limits with output min of platform and programmed size; granule from TG0 with reserved as 64K and host-preferred fallback; start and block levels constrained with base masking, per-level checks, leaf population and contiguity widening; loads and stores endian-aware with CAS.

Host save and restore cover bases, configs, attributes and controls with extended regs only when capable and errata barrier on restore; privileged S1E1 fast path temporarily installs guest protection.

Stage-2 attributes map to combined forms with reserved to non-cacheable; transient normalized, cacheability weakest-wins; device forced outer-shareable with combined preference outer over inner over non; PAR merges attributes, address and shareability with fault handling. PAN3 needs advertisement plus PIE or enhanced control; base permissions from user, read-only and execute-never with hypervisor rules and overlay, further narrowed by hierarchical tables.

locks.text: Forwarding holds ITS mutex across resolve and map; per-interrupt state under raw spinlock with IRQs saved nested inside mutex; teardown uses spinlock plus references.
Descriptor replacement dispatched by CPU capability among unprivileged, LSE or exclusive-loop variants validating user faults and signaling retry.

state_machines.text: Walks advance by level to success, classified fault or contention retry; S1 adds identity success, level-zero size fault, start-level translation fault and filter or nested abort.
Atomic replace yields success, access fault, or mismatch retry; exclusive-loop also retries on failed store-conditional.

structs.text: MMU snapshot holds TTBR0 and TTBR1, TCR, MAIR, TCR2, PIR, PIRE0, POR EL1 and EL0, SCTLR, VTTBR and VTCR.

Hyp width is max of identity and kernel stage-one widths with identity 48 bits; granule selectors map to shifts 12, 14 and 16 with input width 64 minus size; memattr pairs outer and inner nibbles with non-cacheable, write-through, write-back and allocate codes, outer-zero as device; shareability two-bit none, reserved, outer and inner.
